Model, assumptions & limitations

Cooling model: Rθ(Q) = Rmin + (Rno-flow − Rmin) / (1 + (Qcaptured / Qscale)^n); Qcaptured = delivered flow × capture fraction. TCPU = Tinlet + heat load × Rθ. Baseline temperature uses the same rig and the baseline delivered airflow. ΔT = Tbaseline − TCPU; negative values mean worse cooling than the baseline. Default baseline is 80°C at 25°C inlet, 100 W, 0.55°C/W and zero delivered airflow. The coefficients are illustrative and adjustable, not fitted measurements. The pressure input is still a constant pressure requirement, not a full radiator system curve.

Scores: Simple ratio = ΔT / dBA (undefined at nonpositive dBA). Main score = ΔT / 2^((dBA − 30)/10); the energy-based alternative = ΔT / 10^((dBA − 30)/10). The latter uses a relative A-weighted mean-square sound-pressure index, not acoustic watts. A 10 dB increase doubles the main penalty and multiplies the energy penalty by ten. The approximate loudness rule is not a standardized psychoacoustic calculation and is particularly uncertain at quiet levels. Scores exclude room noise and all other fans.

Cooling search: Keeps this shared rig, pressure, target airflow and physical envelope fixed. For each geometry, solves the minimum feasible RPM and samples 12 higher RPMs (rounded to 50 RPM) up to 5,000. Maximizes the main cooling score while meeting flow, temperature, positive cooling improvement and existing geometry constraints. Noise-only mode does not enforce the thermal limit. Comparisons and curves always recompute saved fans under the current shared pressure and thermal setup.

Motion: Rotation integrates θ = 2π × RPM / 60 × time; tonal audio uses blade count × RPM / 60. Preview sound starts rotation; Pause fan stops both. Slow motion scales the visual by 0.02 only, leaving sound at true RPM. Frames cannot resolve every blade passage at high speeds: apparent aliasing or backward motion is a display artifact. This is synchronization by RPM, not an acoustic wave phase simulation.

Thermal context: Noctua on CPU heat load and case airflow. Loudness approximation: NIOSH Industrial Noise Control Manual. These sources do not validate the chosen thermal or scoring coefficients.

Version 1.2 · air density 1.204 kg/m³; speed of sound 343 m/s. Diameter is rotor diameter; shroud inner diameter adds twice the tip clearance. Tip pitch is relative to the plane of rotation; root pitch adds twist. Blades use a smooth, tapered, swept mesh with rounded edges; maximum thickness follows the editor. This is not a validated manufactured airfoil. Housing hardware, supports, finishes and exploded view are visual details only; the screening equations are unchanged.

Tip speed U = πDN/60; blade-passing frequency = blade count × N/60. Annular area A = π(D² − H²)/4. Solidity σ = blade count × chord / mean circumference. Loading = (1 − exp(−1.8σ)) × sin(2α) × stall factor, with α = tip pitch + 0.35 × twist. Leakage = exp(−k × clearance / diameter), with k = 3 for a shroud, otherwise 7 and an additional 0.78 multiplier.

Free-air flow Q₀ = 0.30AU × loading × leakage. Shutoff pressure P₀ = 0.20 × ½ρU² × loading × leakage. Delivered flow Q = Q₀√max(0, 1 − Ptarget/P₀). This assumed parabolic fan curve intersects a constant pressure requirement, not a measured system curve. Maximum flow and maximum pressure never occur together.

Noise uses an arbitrary 30 dB reference at 120 mm / 1,500 RPM, a 50 log₁₀(speed ratio) scaling and heuristic geometry penalties. Broadband energy is distributed across 80 logarithmic bands (20 Hz–20 kHz). Six BPF harmonics fall by 7 log₂(harmonic order) dB; A-weighting is applied to each tone and broadband band before energy summation. Spectrum values are integrated band levels, not dB/Hz. SPL and dBA exclude background noise.

Uncalibrated: no numerical error bounds are available. Absolute levels and geometry rankings need validation against measured fan curves and spectra. Sweep is a simple assumed tonal correction, not a universal noise benefit. Motor/bearing noise, structural vibration, installation, grille/stator interactions, detailed tip vortices and realistic stall are omitted. No structural, motor-power or overspeed analysis is performed. The added thermal model is an uncalibrated steady-state approximation. The optimizer excludes high solidity, strong modeled stall and tip Mach above 0.15; this does not certify a safe physical rotor.

Foundational references: AMCA fan noise and speed scaling · NASA broadband fan noise. These support the physical concepts; they do not validate this prototype’s coefficients.
